answer.rationale: Competitive price cut targeting SMB base with doubled churn conversations requires immediate tactical response. Memory_73 confirms promotional pricing effectiveness for price-sensitive SMB segments with strong acquisition and revenue lift. Memory_57 shows referral incentives work well but are concentrated in established accounts (6+ months), offering limited help for at-risk current customers. Activation messaging (memory_91) and onboarding simplification (memory_31, memory_86) drive engagement but don't directly address price sensitivity. Enterprise sales assist (memory_44) is misaligned with SMB churn risk. Standard experiment scale allows rapid deployment to price-sensitive segment while maintaining control and measurability. Flagged downstream risk: promotional pricing may train customers to expect discounts, potentially reducing willingness-to-pay long-term and creating margin pressure. Uncertainty preserved: we have no direct evidence on pricing elasticity in churn scenarios, competitor response timing, or optimal promotional depth—recommend tiered pricing test to bound risk while responding to immediate threat.
